source_policy: Operator-curated, attribution-preserving public excerpts; refs may be stale; all arms see identical bounded source text; no ground-truth willingness to pay.

cases.question: Should we prioritize a paid services engagement fixing the Open Food Network Canada map opening-view defect? What is the commercially rational next action?

evidence.excerpt: Canada's map was reported to center over Guatemala when a producer location was mis-geocoded to Brazil; fixed zoom also excludes parts of Canada. The issue proposes robust map bounds or configurable center/zoom; the issue was open on 2026-10-23.
Open Food Foundation publishes pathways for developers or system administrators interested in potentially paid contributions; it does not promise compensation for this map issue.
Published contribution onboarding describes an initial volunteer stage and certification criteria for subsequent paid participation; present-day applicability and duration need confirmation.

cases.question: Is fixing Foodsoft's order-balancing mismatch a worthwhile immediate revenue opportunity or only an engineering contribution? What should we do first?

evidence.excerpt: A report demonstrates quantities displayed to three decimal places yet compared to an unrounded sum (e.g. 1.308 versus 1.307692), yielding an incorrect mismatch indicator. An adjustment and regression test are possible.
Foodsoft is open software for cooperative ordering, shared accounting, and jobs. Availability of code or community issue does not establish payment for a specific repair.

cases.question: Should we build a paid independent rooftop-solar performance assessment service using pvlib? Identify the most defensible first commercial experiment.

evidence.excerpt: US Department of Energy describes already available PV monitoring platforms, performance indicators and independent third-party monitoring. Routine monitoring is an established service category.

Solargis advertises independent PV performance assessment combining measured generation with modeled production cases and underperformance analysis. This offering substantially overlaps a proposed audit.

pvlib-python supplies open-source photovoltaic simulation and performance modeling functions. The software is a useful model component, not a finished site-specific certified audit or evidence of a local buyer.

cases.question: Should we productize KoboToolbox as a Taiwan free-roaming dog population survey service? Which technical and buyer evidence is still missing?

evidence.excerpt: Free-roaming dog abundance studies using repeated sightings/capture-recapture rely on suitably identifying individuals and defensible estimation assumptions.

Taiwan periodically estimates free-roaming dog populations; periodic aggregate surveys are not a live system of individual dog re-identification. No agency's purchase decision is established by this survey.
KoboToolbox provides offline data collection, survey forms, exports, and attachments. It is not a proven turnkey photographic dog re-identification and population-estimation application.
